CARDIOLOGY NOTE   Date: 2026-05-25
56F, ambulatory visit for a scheduled cardiology problem evaluation.

S:
Patient returns to cardiology clinic for follow-up. She reports that walking more than one block or climbing a single flight leaves her winded and that she now sleeps on two pillows. Over the past month her exertional tolerance has declined. She has been weighing herself daily and following the low-sodium plan. She reports being unable to keep a regular work schedule and missed 9 days of work last month. She works as a school cafeteria aide and has struggled with the standing and lifting. Appetite is fair. Taking medications as prescribed. Mother with rheumatoid arthritis. Lives with her adult daughter, who assists at home.

O:
BP 122/78, HR 82, RR 18, Temp 98.1 F, SpO2 96% on room air. Weight 171 lb, up 3 lb from prior.
General: mild distress with exertion, comfortable at rest.
CV: regular rate, soft S3, no rub.
Lungs: bibasilar fine crackles.
Extremities: 1+ bilateral ankle edema.
Labs (this week): Hgb 10.9 g/dL, A1c 6.0%, BNP elevated from baseline, creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, potassium 4.4 mmol/L.

A/P:
1. Chronic congestive heart failure with NYHA class III symptoms. Increase loop diuretic and recheck electrolytes in one week. Continue guideline-directed therapy; reinforced daily weights and fluid and sodium limits. Cardiac rehabilitation referral discussed.
2. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks and adding short walks as tolerated. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
3. Anemia, stable on recheck. Continue oral iron daily with vitamin C. Repeat CBC in 3 months.
4. Family history: discussed mother's history and reassured patient regarding her own current concerns.
5. Function and work: reduced tolerance is affecting her usual schedule. Provided a letter describing current activity limits for her employer.

Return to clinic in 2 weeks to review response to diuretic changes, sooner for worsening breathlessness or swelling.
